_description: Disclosed pre-existing debt for VG-CATALOG-RULE-UNIQUE (item 18.37, SPEC §7.3): a committed list of rung-2 control pairs that already shared an identical shape and fixture set when the gate was built, so a buyer reading one control's result may in fact be reading another's rule under its own title. A pair listed here does not fail the gate; any pair NOT listed here does, including a NEW duplicate introduced after this file was written -- in any catalog under spec/catalogs/{base,overlays}, not just the ones named here (the check driver discovers catalogs from the directory tree). This file is meant to shrink, never grow: each pair is paid down by its own item (18.37a DOC-01, 18.37b ROB-02, 18.37c the remaining 24 eu-ai-act pairs), which removes that pair here as part of its own fix; a baseline entry that stops being a real duplicate must be removed, not left stale -- the gate fails on that too. Pairs are unordered two-element arrays of control ids, sorted, and each group of identical rules is keyed to its first control, so paying down one control of a group of three or more can re-key that group's remaining pairs. The four overlays (conduct, employment, finance, insurance) have zero duplicate pairs today; they are listed for the same reason nist-ai-rmf is: so an empty entry is a confirmed fact, not an assumption. ``ceilings`` pins each catalog's pair count at today's disclosed total so the gate also catches the common bypass the pair-level checks alone miss: quietly adding a new duplicate to ``pairs`` without also raising the matching ceiling. It does not stop a change that deliberately edits both fields together in the same diff -- that is a reviewable, visible edit, not a silent one, and is the residual risk this mechanism accepts. Lowering a ceiling to match a real pay-down is expected and required; raising one needs its own harness/decisions/phase-18.tsv row, the same as any other debt-file change.
